summary: The incident began when the external payment service provider (PSP) experienced high latency, causing requests to pile up in the payments service. Under the memory-constrained 128Mi limit, the backup of concurrent requests triggered severe CPU throttling (due to Go GC thrashing) and OOM kills. An operator attempt to mitigate this by tightening the gateway timeout to 80ms backfired, introducing a high rate of user-visible 5xx errors until it was reverted.

alerts.name: PodCrashLooping
alerts.summary: payments: container restarted 4.116 times in 10 minutes

hypotheses.summary: The external payment provider (PSP) became slow, with responses taking ~1.1s. This caused concurrent requests and goroutines to back up in the payments service, triggering extreme CPU throttling (due to GC thrashing under memory pressure) and eventual OOMKilled crashes.

evidence.shows: The earliest signs of slow requests (~1000-1200ms) on the payments service.
The external payment provider (PSP) is taking over 1 second to respond, causing the slowness.
The accumulation of inflight requests led to severe memory pressure (229% of limit) and CPU throttling (89.3% before restarts), leading to probe timeouts and OOMKilled terminations.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Contact the payment service provider to resolve their latency, and temporarily scale up the memory/CPU limits of the payments service (or implement load shedding) to handle buffered inflight requests without GC thrashing and OOMKilled crashes.

hypotheses.summary: An operator tried to 'protect the edge' by reducing the gateway's UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS to 80ms, which caused immediate timeouts on upstream checkouts (which take longer under PSP latency), leading to a spike in gateway errors until reverted.

evidence.shows: An operator deployed a config change tightening the gateway upstream timeout to 80ms.
The 80ms timeout was far too short, causing almost all upstream orders/checkout requests to instantly fail.
The change was reverted to restore the 4000ms timeout, resolving the high error rate at the gateway.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Avoid changing timeouts to aggressively low values (such as 80ms) during active incidents without verifying downstream request processing times.
